articles.description:
What is Google Discover?

Google Discover is a personalized feed that showcases relevant content to users based on their search history, location, and interests. It was first introduced in 2018 and has since become a significant part of the Google search experience. Discover allows users to explore topics they're interested in, and it's also a great way for publishers to reach their target audience.

What's Changing?

Google has been making significant changes to Google Discover in recent times. One of the most notable changes is the introduction of a more personalized feed, which is based on the user's search history and interests. This means that users will see more relevant content in their Discover feed, and publishers will have a better chance of reaching their target audience. Additionally, Google has also introduced a new feature that allows users to customize their Discover feed by selecting topics they're interested in.

Implications and Conclusion

The implications of these changes are significant, and they have the potential to revolutionize the way publishers reach their target audience. With a more personalized feed, users are more likely to engage with content that's relevant to them, and publishers can increase their visibility and reach. Additionally, the new feature that allows users to customize their Discover feed gives publishers more control over their content and allows them to target their audience more effectively. Overall, these changes are a positive step forward for Google Discover, and they have the potential to make it an even more powerful tool for publishers and users alike.

articles.author: david duymelinck
articles.description:
I have been waiting for the new release, because it has PHP 8.5 support.
I recommend to use PIE. The main reason is that you can use it on all the OS's. So not need to figure out how the extension needs to be installed on your OS. 
The one gotcha I encountered was not finding phpize. For the people that are not familiar with the command, it is a part of the php-dev package, and it is build for a specific PHP version. The great thing about the package is that you can add the version, php8.5-dev, so that a phpize command is created with that version, phpize8.5. For PIE the name of the command doesn't matter.
The installation command is simply pie install xdebug/xdebug. Run php --version to verify xdebug is enabled. And optionally check the config file if you need to make changes.
I'm still exploring the debug possibilities. But for the pipe operator it can intercept the intermediate values, that is cool.
Happy debugging!
articles.title: Php quickie: Xdebug 3.5 is out
